subject.title: [Feature]: Automatic Output Sanitization for Sensitive Data

question: Should OpenClaw add a core automatic final-output sensitive-data sanitizer, or keep this policy plugin-owned through message hooks, and what default scope/config should apply?
rationale: The request mutates user-visible output and overlaps logging/tool redaction, SecretRefs, plugin message hooks, channel delivery, and provider/tool behavior, so automation should not choose the boundary or defaults.

options.title: Design a core boundary
options.body: Define a security-reviewed core sanitizer that reuses existing redaction infrastructure and starts with documented, tested scope across final replies and selected adjacent sinks.

options.title: Use plugin hooks first
options.body: Keep core policy minimal and add only missing extension points so an official or community sanitizer plugin owns detection and output mutation.

options.title: Document existing limits
options.body: Decline broad automatic final-output filtering for now and document reliance on SecretRefs, log/tool redaction, local isolation, skills, and plugins.

recommendation.title: Design a core boundary
recommendation.body: Define a security-reviewed core sanitizer that reuses existing redaction infrastructure and starts with documented, tested scope across final replies and selected adjacent sinks.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is security-boundary policy and CODEOWNERS routes adjacent secrets/security surfaces to this group.
